intended_object: The canonical inclusion ring homomorphism ⋂_j O_{v_j} ↪ O_{v_i}, from the intersection of the valuation rings of a family of valuations on a field K into the valuation ring of the i-th valuation. Inferred from the docstring and from the companion definition `intersectionSubring`.
explanation:
`intersectionSubring val` is defined as the infimum ⨅ i, (val i).valuationSubring, and the file proves that x is in it iff val i x ≤ 1 for every i. The definition applies Mathlib's `Subring.inclusion` to the inclusion `intersectionSubring val ≤ (val i).valuationSubring`, and that inclusion follows directly from the membership lemma. So the map is exactly the canonical inclusion of the common integers into one valuation ring. The library confirms this: it proves the map is the identity on underlying elements of K and that it is injective, and uses it to give the algebra structure.

The setting is reasonable. K is any field, ι is any index type with no finiteness assumption, and the value group is any linearly ordered commutative group with zero. Requiring one common Γ₀ for the whole family is the usual convention for families of valuations and is not a real restriction here.

Mathlib has no specific declaration for this map. It is an instance of the general `Subring.inclusion`, which the definition uses directly.
